chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Dawud ibn Sirhan, who said:

I saw Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) measuring dates with his hand. So I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! If you could have ordered one of your sons, or one of your slaves, so they would have sufficed for you.' So he said: 'O Dawud! It is not correct for the Muslim person except three: understanding in the Religion, and patience upon the calamity, and good management regarding the livelihood.'
ai.seo_question: What are the three essential qualities for a Muslim according to Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the Imam’s personal engagement in economic transactions to ensure fairness and avoid the arrogance of delegation, a practice rooted in the Shia emphasis on *adl* (justice) in daily dealings. The three virtues cited—*taffahum* (deep religious understanding), *sabr* (patience in adversity), and *husn al-taqdir* (prudent management of livelihood)—form a holistic framework for spiritual and material success, linking inner piety with practical stewardship of resources.

en.hubeali: Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Dawood Bin Sirham who said,

‘I saw Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> weighing dates with his<sup>asws</sup> hand. So I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! If you<sup>asws</sup> could have ordered one of your<sup>asws</sup> sons, or one of your slaves, so they would have sufficed for you<sup>asws</sup>’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O Dawood! It is not correct for the Muslim person except three – the pondering in the Religion, and the patience upon the calamities, and improving the management regarding the livelihood’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ahmad ibn Muhammad has narrated from ibn Faddal from Dawud ibn Sarhan who has said the following: “

I saw abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, measure dates with his own hands; and I said, ‘I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause, I wish you would have ordered certain persons of your servants or sons to help you.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘O Dawud, a Muslim cannot achieve a proper condition without three things: proper understanding of religion, exercising patience in hardships, and proper planning for his living and sustenance.’”
